name: Feature Prioritization
summary: Ranks candidate features by evidence of customer need, effort and strategic fit, with the reasoning shown.
description: Scores each candidate feature on reach, impact, confidence in the evidence and effort, using the customer evidence you provide (interview themes, requests, usage notes). Shows the scoring inputs next to each rank so you can disagree with them. It does not invent demand: a feature with no supporting evidence is ranked as unvalidated, not low.
problems: I don't know which feature to build next
Everyone on the team wants something different on the roadmap
I need to justify roadmap decisions with evidence

inputs.label: Candidate features
inputs.description: Features you are considering, one per line.
inputs.example:
Bulk invoice import
Slack alerts for overdue invoices

inputs.label: Customer evidence
inputs.description: Interview themes, support tickets, requests or usage data that bear on the candidates.
inputs.example: 9 of 12 interviewees mentioned manual imports as their biggest time sink.

inputs.label: Team capacity
inputs.description: Roughly how much the team can build in the next cycle.

outputs.label: Ranked features
outputs.description: Each feature with reach, impact, evidence confidence, effort and final rank.

outputs.label: Rationale
outputs.description: Why the top items rank where they do and what would change the order.

steps.name: Score features
steps.responsibility: Estimate reach, impact and effort for each candidate, citing the evidence used.

steps.name: Rank
steps.responsibility: Compute scores deterministically from the estimates and sort them.

dependencies.reason: Interview themes are strong evidence of customer need.

criteria.description: Every score above 'low' confidence cites supplied evidence.
Every candidate feature appears in the ranking exactly once.
